statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-26458 is a memory leak in xdr_rmtcallres() in libgssrpc (src/lib/rpc/pmap_rmt.c): the decoded port pointer is stored only after the following field also decodes, so it leaks if that decode fails. MIT fixed it in commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/c5f9c816107f70139de11b38aa02db2f1774ee0d , first released in krb5 1.22, whose message describes the function as unused within the krb5 tree. Debian marks both trixie versions, 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 and the 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 security update, vulnerable with urgency unimportant: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2024-26458 . This owner is built from those Debian versions. The MIT 1.21.3 source of xdr_rmtcallres() lacks the change, and neither Debian's patches for 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 nor this owner's own backports touch pmap_rmt.c, so every build carries the leak. In every build in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64, libgssrpc.so.4.2 in libgssrpc4t64 exports the function as gssrpc_xdr_rmtcallres with an unchanged size across every build of each architecture. Pending: a decision whether to backport the upstream change or to record MIT's reasoning; because the function is exported, code outside the krb5 tree can call it, and a not-affected statement needs a recorded maintainer decision.
